[Meeting header] 2025-03-03 15:00 PST | 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Ethan Moore (Avalon Head of Platform), Priya Patel (SRE), Carlos Mendes (Security Lead)

Summary: quick execution-focused onboarding. Confirm VPC options, security controls, perf baseline and ramp plan. Agreed pilot for dedicated capacity with private control plane, 4-week ramp to staging.

Topics: introductions; current infra; security/compliance; network and data residency; performance testing plan; rollout and success criteria; docs & deliverables

Action items: see action_items metadata above.

[00:00] Jordan Kim: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick intros then i'll run through the runbook we shared.  i think we have about 55 minutes so we'll try to leave 10 for Q&A.
[00:18] Ethan Moore: hey, ethan here, we run platform at avalon freight. our main goals are: reduce latency in routing assistant, keep pii off public endpoints, and predictable cost. timeline: pilot in next two weeks, prod in ~6-8 weeks.
[00:35] Priya Patel: priya, SRE. our stack is k8s on aws, we use private subnets, strict egress rules, vpn to vendors. we need V P C peering or private link, and we can't leak logs to vendor-managed s3 buckets without encryption + audit.
[00:50] Carlos Mendes: carlos, security. SOC2 in flight, we need K M S integration, H S M for keys ideally, and data residency in us-east-1 for some flows.
[01:10] Maya Singh: thanks — from redwood's side, we generally support hosted api, dedicated capacity, and private deployment. for this pilot given rexquirements it sounds like dedicated with private control plane or private deployment on your V P C is the likely path.  we can do VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink. there are tradeoffs re latency and ops burden.
[01:45] Ethan Moore: can you clarify the difference? like if we go dedicated vs private, what changes for us day-to-day?
[02:02] Jordan Kim: good question. dedicated is our reserved GPU pool managed by redwood — you get isolated capacity and predictable throughput, but control plane is hosted. private deployment gives you the control plane in your V P C or on-prem, so you manage keys, audit logs, etc. dedicated is faster to stand up; private is best for strict compliance.
[02:30] Priya Patel: latency and egress concern — which one keeps traffic inside our network? private deployment, right?
[02:40] Maya Singh: correct. private keeps everything in your V P C. dedicated means the model inference happens on our infra, so you'll have outbound connections; we do offer V P C peering to keep hops minimal but egress still crosses boundaries.
[03:05] Ethan Moore: what's the typical latency delta we should expect?
[03:12] Maya Singh: depends on region and model. ballpark: dedicated with peering in same region adds ~10-30ms median compared to fully private on-prem. if you're doing sub-100ms SLOs we recommend private deployment or colocated dedicated.
[03:40] Carlos Mendes: ok, encryption at rest and in transit — do you support customer-managed keys (K M S / H S M)?
[03:50] Jordan Kim: yes; we support K M S integrations and can work with BYOK patterns, and H S M in private deployments. we'll share the key management architecture doc after the call.
[04:05] Priya Patel: audit logs — we need an immutable audit trail for model access and prompt history. can that be exported to our SIEM?
[04:18] Maya Singh: yes, we can stream audit events to your logging endpoint (SPLUNK/Kinesis) and also provide a downloadable audit bundle. there are retention settings as well.
[04:33] Ethan Moore: on performance — we want to baseline cost/latency for our routing assistant which does 4k-8k token prompts. what's your plan?
[04:45] Maya Singh: we'll run a throughput test against a representative prompt set. plan: maya runs a 50k-token workload across a few model variants on our dedicated infra to measure tokens/sec, median latency, and cost per 1k tokens. i'll upload results and a spreadsheet.
[05:05] Jordan Kim: we'll also include KV cache and batching tuning recommendations — for your workload we expect prefix caching to reduce repeated context tokens by up to 40%.
[05:22] Priya Patel: curious about quantization / model variants — do you have recommendations for balancing cost vs quality?
[05:32] Maya Singh: yes, our optimize team maintains profiles. for routing use-cases we often suggest a quantized 8-bit variant for cheaper inference and a full-fp16 for critical escalation flows. we can A/B these in the pilot.
[05:50] Ethan Moore: what's the SLA for dedicated? and are there runbooks for failover?
[05:58] Jordan Kim: dedicated comes with a 99.9% uptime SLA and runbooks. we also support automatic fallback to hosted model variants if capacity issues arise — can set a policy per-route.
[06:12] Carlos Mendes: procurement and legal will want standard terms and data processing addendum. can you attach that?
[06:20] Jordan Kim: yes, i'll share our enterprise contract and DPA. will send links in follow-up.
[06:30] Priya Patel: on networking, we need the sample terraform and the CIDR ranges.
[06:36] Maya Singh: noted. we'll include a terraform snippet for peering and the ip ranges. also a checklist for security review.
[06:50] Ethan Moore: success criteria — we'll judge by: 1) <120ms p95 for our routing API, 2) 30% reduction in cost per request compared to current on-prem benchmark, 3) no PII leakage in logs.
[07:10] Jordan Kim: sounds good. pilot plan: week 0-1: network and infra setup, week 1-2: perf baseline and tuning, week 3: integrate into staging, week 4: validate SLOs and handoff to ops.
[07:28] Maya Singh: i'll run the perf tests starting Friday. jordan will send security docs and terraform. can we schedule a 30-minute check-in next Monday?
[07:40] Ethan Moore: yes monday 11am works for us.
[07:50] Jordan Kim: great. any last questions?
[07:55] Carlos Mendes: one — can you certify the service for our SOC2 auditor or provide evidence?
[08:04] Jordan Kim: we can provide SOC2 report and a control mappings pack; we'll redact any customer-specific material.
[08:18] Priya Patel: thanks, appreciate the clarity.

[Recap 50:00] Jordan Kim: recap of next steps: send network terraform and security pack (Jordan), run perf benchmark and upload results (Maya), Avalon to confirm SSO and compliance contact (Ethan). schedule check-in monday 11am PT. Links: onboarding runbook: https://redwood.com/onboarding/avalon (internal), security pack: https://redwood.com/security/smallpack (shared link), perf spreadsheet template: https://redwood.com/benchmarks/template.xlsx

[54:30] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript: auto-generated; some proper nouns may be transcribed slightly incorrectly (e.g., KMS as K M S, VPC as V P C).
